newsitem.title: CANADA: Noranda Q4 sinks on low commodities prices.
newsitem.headline: Noranda Q4 sinks on low commodities prices.

text.p: Noranda Inc said on Thursday that lower prices for base metals and some forestry products cut into its fourth-quarter and full-year profits.
Copper, aluminum, nickel and oriented strand board prices were 10 to 20 percent lower in 1996 compared to 1995, Noranda said.

Pulp prices were more than 40 percent lower than in 1995, the company added. Noranda also cited a slightly stronger Canadian dollar and market-related downtime at several Noranda Forest Inc mills as areason for lower 1996 earnings,
Noranda Forest is about 66 percent-owned by Noranda.
But higher oil, gas and lumber prices as well as cost reductions and lower interest rates helped the company's fourth-quarter and full-year earnings, Noranda said.

"Notwithstanding the decline in earnings, 1996 was a successful year in terms of positioning the company for future growth in both assets and earnings," Noranda chief executive David Kerr said in a statement.
Noranda said that fourth-quarter earnings fell to C$36 million or C$0.12 a share from year earlier C$111 million or C$0.41 a share.
Noranda's full-year net earnings fell to C$254 million or C$1.02 a share from C$524 million or C$2.19 a share in 1995.
The Toronto-based natural resource company said it had C$1.7 billion of capital expenditures in 1996, before asset sales of C$0.7 billion.
Noranda said it expected to benefit in 1997 from sustained growth in developed and developing countries as well as improving commodities prices.
"During the year, we expect to see price improvements for a number of our products, including aluminum, nickel, zinc and newsprint," Kerr said.
